gracilisuchus:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: General pseudosuchian research)

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus is an extinct genus of small pseudosuchians that lived in Argentina during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Gracilisuchus (meaning "slender crocodile") is an extinct genus of tiny pseudosuchian (a group which includes the ancestors of crocodilians) from the Late Triassic of Argentina.

facts.statement: Alfred Romer first described the genus and species Gracilisuchus stipanicicorum in 1972.
facts.quote: Both the genus and the species were first described by Alfred Romer in 1972.

facts.statement: The holotype of Gracilisuchus was discovered during a 1964–1965 expedition in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin of La Rioja Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: A four-month expedition spanning 1964 and 1965 in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin of La Rioja Province, Argentina was conducted by Alfred Romer and his colleagues

facts.statement: The Gracilisuchus holotype was found approximately 3 km north of the Chañares River.
facts.quote: Among these was the skeleton of a small suchian archosaur, discovered about 3 km north of the Chañares River.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is currently housed at the Museum of Paleontology at the National University of La Rioja with the catalog number PULR 08.
facts.quote: The specimen has since been transferred to the Museum of Paleontology at the National University of La Rioja (PULR), where it bears the specimen number PULR 08.

facts.statement: José Bonaparte collected additional Gracilisuchus specimens at the site between 1970 and 1972.
facts.quote: José Bonaparte from the Miguel Lillo Institute (PVL) later collected additional material from the site between 1970 and 1972, including two new specimens

facts.statement: Alfred Romer described the Gracilisuchus specimens in the journal Breviora in 1972.
facts.quote: In 1972, Romer described the specimens his team had discovered in the journal Breviora.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus contains only one species, G. stipanicicorum, which belongs to the clade Suchia near the ancestry of crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, G. stipanicicorum, which is placed in the clade Suchia, close to the ancestry of crocodylomorphs.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus was a small member of the Pseudosuchia.
facts.quote: Gracilisuchus was a small member of the Pseudosuchia.

facts.statement: The largest known skull of Gracilisuchus measures slightly over 9 cm in length, and the largest femur is roughly 8 cm long.
facts.quote: The largest skull has a length of slightly over 9 cm, and the largest femur has a length of roughly 8 cm.

facts.statement: Alfred Romer estimated the total length of Gracilisuchus at 21 cm in 1972, while a 2014 study estimated the body length (excluding hip and tail) at 28 cm.
facts.quote: In 1972, Alfred Romer estimated a total length of 21 cm; in 2014, Agustinia Lecuona and Julia Desojo estimated a length of 28 cm for the body excluding the hip and tail.

facts.statement: The estimated weight of Gracilisuchus is 1.31 kg.
facts.quote: The weight of Gracilisuchus has been estimated at 1.31 kg.

facts.statement: The supratemporal fenestra of Gracilisuchus is uniquely wider than it is long.
facts.quote: Additionally, the supratemporal fenestra is, uniquely, wider than it is long.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus possesses a scleral ring in the eye socket where the bony segments contact but do not overlap.
facts.quote: Within the eye socket, there is a scleral ring, and the ossicles (bony segments) comprising the ring contact but do not overlap each other.

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives Turfanosuchus and Yonghesuchus, the lacrimal bone of Gracilisuchus is as tall as the eye socket, a trait convergent with Tropidosuchus, early theropods, and crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: Unlike its closest relatives, Turfanosuchus and Yonghesuchus, but convergent upon Tropidosuchus, early theropods, and the Crocodylomorpha, the lacrimal bone is as tall as the eye socket instead of being significantly shorter.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus has a small, triangular postparietal bone.
facts.quote: There is also a postparietal bone, which is small and triangular.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus has four teeth in the premaxilla, unlike Turfanosuchus and Yonghesuchus which have five.
facts.quote: Also unlike Turfanosuchus and Yonghesuchus, Gracilisuchus has four teeth in the premaxilla instead of five, like Prestosuchus, Saurosuchus, Fasolasuchus, Batrachotomus, the Rauisuchidae, and the Crocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: The premaxillary teeth of Gracilisuchus lack a cutting edge (carina) and serrated denticles on their front or rear edges.
facts.quote: There is no cutting edge, or carina, at the front of the premaxillary teeth, and they lack serrated denticles on either the front or rear edges.

facts.statement: A vertebral series originally thought to belong to the tail of Gracilisuchus has been reassigned to the genus Tropidosuchus.
facts.quote: A vertebral series ("Series A"), originally identified as the tail of Gracilisuchus, has been reassigned to Tropidosuchus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether a scapula and coracoid found overlapping the holotype belong to a second Gracilisuchus individual or are associated debris.
facts.quote: A scapula and coracoid overlapping the holotype's limb bones likely belongs to a second Gracilisuchus.

facts.statement: Incomplete anatomical knowledge of Gracilisuchus hampered research until it was redescribed in papers published in 2011 and 2017.
facts.quote: The lack of complete knowledge regarding its anatomy hampered subsequent studies of Gracilisuchus, until papers from Lecuona, Desojo, and Diego Pol in 2011 and 2017 redescribed its remains.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus possessed eight cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: There are eight cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus had sixteen dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: There are sixteen dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Two sacral vertebrae have been identified in Gracilisuchus.
facts.quote: Two sacral vertebrae are known.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus had at least 16 caudal (tail) vertebrae.
facts.quote: There were at least 16 caudal (tail) vertebrae.

facts.statement: The distal end of the Gracilisuchus humerus is 2.5 times wider than its shaft.
facts.quote: The width of the bottom end of the humerus is 2.5 times that of the shaft

facts.statement: The separation between the two halves of the Gracilisuchus ischium is only 22% of the bone's total length.
facts.quote: The articulation between the two halves of the ischium is characteristically close to the top of the bone, with the separated portion being only 22% the length of the bone

facts.statement: The bottom 55% of the Gracilisuchus femur is bowed, creating a sigmoidal shape.
facts.quote: Roughly the bottom 55% of the femur is bowed, resulting in a sigmoidal shape.

facts.statement: The Gracilisuchus tibia is 90% the length of the femur.
facts.quote: The tibia is 90% of the femur's length

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus had five toes with a preserved phalangeal count of 2-3-2-2-1.
facts.quote: There are five digits in the foot, with the number of phalanges being preserved on each digit being 2-3-2-2-1 from the first digit to the fifth

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ornithosuchus shares the close articulation between ischium halves seen in Gracilisuchus.
facts.quote: Ornithosuchus may have a similar condition

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus had two rows of osteoderms on its neck and torso starting just behind the skull.
facts.quote: Gracilisuchus bore two rows of bony plates known as osteoderms above its neck and torso, with the first pair beginning immediately behind the skull.

facts.statement: The front row of Gracilisuchus osteoderms were triangular while the rear ones were leaf-shaped.
facts.quote: While osteoderms from the frontmost row are triangular, osteoderms further behind are leaf-shaped.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus osteoderms show variable surface textures, ranging from smooth to having radial pits and grooves.
facts.quote: Different specimens of Gracilisuchus have different osteoderm surface textures; some are smooth like Turfanosuchus, while others bear radial pits and grooves like Erpetosuchus.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus was described by Romer in 1972.
facts.quote: By the time of Romer's description of Gracilisuchus in 1972, the geographic range of ornithosuchids had expanded to include the Argentinian Venaticosuchus and Riojasuchus, which had been referred to the family by Bonaparte in 1969.

facts.statement: Romer classified Gracilisuchus as a relative of Ornithosuchus based on skull and skeletal similarities.
facts.quote: Romer considered Gracilisuchus to be, "quite clear[ly]", a relative of the Scottish Ornithosuchus, owing to similarities in skull structure and other skeletal features.

facts.statement: Romer debated whether ornithosuchids were dinosaurs, citing basal archosaur traits like a closed acetabulum and osteoderms.
facts.quote: However, he had reservations regarding Walker's identification of ornithosuchids as dinosaurs, noting basal archosaur traits such as the closed acetabulum, osteoderms, and crocodile-normal ankle.

facts.statement: Cruickshank removed Gracilisuchus from Ornithosuchidae because it had a crocodile-normal ankle unlike other ornithosuchids.
facts.quote: He observed that, while Gracilisuchus had a "crocodile-normal" joint, other ornithosuchids had a "crocodile-reversed" joint; he thus removed Gracilisuchus from the Ornithosuchidae.

facts.statement: Brinkman debated whether Gracilisuchus was a derived ornithosuchid or part of a separate evolutionary radiation.
facts.quote: According to Brinkman, this left two possibilities: either Gracilisuchus was derived from the basal ornithosuchid condition in a manner different from other ornithosuchids, or it represents a different evolutionary radiation altogether, separate from the ornithosuchids.

facts.statement: Brinkman tentatively placed Gracilisuchus closer to crocodile-line archosaurs like Erythrosuchidae and Rauisuchidae than to Ornithosuchidae.
facts.quote: Thus, in a phylogenetic tree, Brinkman tentatively depicted Gracilisuchus as being closer to the "crocodile-line" Erythrosuchidae, the Rauisuchidae, and the Stagonolepididae (=Aetosauria) than the Ornithosuchidae and the Euparkeriidae.

facts.statement: Benton and Clark classified Gracilisuchus as a member of Suchia in 1988 based on a crocodile-normal ankle.
facts.quote: In 1988, Michael Benton and James Clark published a phylogenetic analysis incorporating Gracilisuchus and 16 other taxa. It was recovered as a member of the Suchia, a group defined by Bernard Krebs as being characterized by a "crocodile-normal" ankle, among other characteristics.

facts.statement: Sereno and Arcucci suggested in 1990 that ornithosuchids including Gracilisuchus were closer to crocodile-line archosaurs than dinosaurs.
facts.quote: In 1990, Paul Sereno and Andrea Arcucci suggested that ornithosuchids - in which they included Gracilisuchus - were actually closer to the conventional "crocodile-line" archosaurs than dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Sereno removed Gracilisuchus from ornithosuchids in 1991 and used it to define the contents of Suchia.
facts.quote: This classification was further revised by Sereno in 1991, when he removed Gracilisuchus from the ornithosuchids, and used it to define Suchia's contents.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus was a small animal measuring approximately 70 centimeters in length and 30 centimeters in height.
facts.quote: Animal de pequeñas dimensiones, media alrededor de 70 centímetros de largo por 30 de alto.

facts.statement: Its skull was low and elongated, triangular in dorsal view with a very narrow anterior end and a wide base.
facts.quote: El cráneo es bajo y alargado, en vista dorsal es triangular, con el extremo anterior muy angosto y la base ancha.

facts.statement: Its large eye orbits projected dorsally, suggesting laterodorsal and rostral eye placement, possibly with considerable visual field overlap.
facts.quote: Sus grandes órbitas oculares se proyectan hacia la dorsal, por lo que los ojos se proyectarían laterodorsal y rostralmente, tal vez con considerable superposición de los campos visuales.

facts.statement: It had a marked reduction in forelimbs, which were 40% shorter than the hind limbs, suggesting it could run upright on its hind legs.
facts.quote: Gracilisuchus poseía una marcada reducción de los miembros anteriores que eran un 40% menores que los miembros posteriores, por lo que se piensa que podía correr erguido en sus patas traseras.

facts.statement: It was a small predator whose diet consisted mainly of insects and small vertebrates.
facts.quote: Se trató de un pequeño depredador cuyo principal alimento estaría constituido principalmente de insectos y vertebrados pequeños.

facts.statement: It was protected by a double row of bony plates running from its spine to the tip of its tail.
facts.quote: protegido por una fila doble de las placas óseas que recorrían su espina dorsal hasta la extremidad de la cola.

facts.statement: Gracilisuchus was described by A. S. Romer in 1972.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por A. S. Romer en 1972

facts.statement: It lived during the middle Triassic, specifically the Anisian and Ladinian stages, approximately 240 to 235 million years ago in what is now South America.
facts.quote: vivió a mediados del período Triásico, en el Anisiense y Ladiniense hace aproximadamente entre 240 y 235 millones de años en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Its fossils were found in the Los Chañares Formation in La Rioja Province, in the Cuyo region of Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en la Formación Los Chañares de la Provincia de La Rioja, en la región cuyana de la Argentina.

facts.statement: It is now considered a sister taxon to the Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: ahora se le considera un taxón hermano de los Crocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Gracilisuchus is Romer, 1972.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Romer, 1972

facts.statement: The only known species is G. stipanicicorum.
facts.quote: species: G. stipanicicorum

facts.statement: The time range for Gracilisuchus is the Ladinian stage, from 241.464 to 237 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Ladinian (241.464 to 237 million years ago)

facts.statement: Later assessments suggested that strong support for certain groupings involving Gracilisuchus may have resulted from poor sampling of non-rauisuchian taxa.
facts.quote: Later assessment noted that this may have resulted from poor non-rauisuchian sampling.
